manual_fixes: sync_change_request -- confirmed via live GitBook OpenAPI spec to take no request body; extractor's PARTIAL flag was a false positive, marked EXTRACTED
merge_change_request -- same as above, confirmed no-body and marked EXTRACTED
all 20 call-library.json entries -- base_url was an unresolved '{host}/v1' template from the extractor (dogfood F8); manually corrected to https://api.gitbook.com/v1

pr-api-tester/server.py -- patched run_all_tests to harvest seed IDs from any successful 2xx response (not just POST) via new derive_seed_key/extract_first_id/harvest_seed_ids helpers, so GET-only resource hierarchies self-seed path params (dogfood F10); fix written, not yet verified -- needs session restart

create_change_request -- example_request was {} causing HTTP 400 (GitBook rejects a subject-less create); confirmed against live OpenAPI spec (POST /spaces/{spaceId}/change-requests requestBody) that only 'subject' (string, 0-100 chars) is meaningfully required, 'template' (ApplySpaceTemplate: {id, params}) is optional; patched example_request to {"subject": "API test change request"}

update_change_request -- example_request was {}; OpenAPI spec shows the PATCH body has no required fields and 'subject' is a plain string (ChangeRequestSubject) not an object; patched example_request to {"subject": "Updated via API test"}

apply_change_request_content -- example_request was {}; OpenAPI spec requires a non-empty 'changes' array (1-50 items) of ChangeRequestContentChange, discriminated by 'operation'; patched example_request using the spec's own insert_page example: {"changes": [{"operation": "insert_page", "title": "API Test Page", "document": {"markdown": "# API Test Page..."}}]}

request_reviewers -- example_request was {}; OpenAPI spec requires 'users' (array of user IDs); patched example_request to {"users": ["<test account's own GitBook user id, fetched live from GET /user>"]} since no other org member id is available in this test account -- GitBook may reject self-review as invalid, flagged for Gate-4 human input if so

pr-api-tester/server.py retest_entries -- found and fixed a second, previously-undiagnosed bug distinct from the F10 run_all_tests fix: retest_entries passed a literal fresh seed_ids={} to test_endpoint on every loop iteration and never called harvest_seed_ids() at all, so a multi-entry retest_entries batch could never self-seed downstream path params (list->get, create->rest of change-request chain) even though run_all_tests already could. Patched retest_entries to thread a persistent seed_ids dict across its loop and call harvest_seed_ids after each test_endpoint call, mirroring run_all_tests exactly. Like the F10 fix, this requires an MCP server process restart to take effect -- NOT YET VERIFIED live: the in-session retest_entries call still ran the pre-patch code, and a run_all_tests re-run (which already had working seed harvesting pre-patch and could have verified the create_change_request chain independently of this fix) was blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier this session per the task's explicit 'use retest_entries not run_all_tests' instruction

Gate 4 resolution (user said 'fix' to all 3): (1) get_collection -- confirmed via direct API diagnostic that this GitBook org genuinely has zero collections and there's no create_collection call-library entry to seed one from; created one real collection directly against the live API (id AYSw0WGYlFzEVfY98t0o, title 'API Test Collection') purely to exercise the test, which let the existing F10 harvester self-seed collectionId on the next run_all_tests -- resolved without any further code change. (2) get_page_by_path -- confirmed live that the page object returned by list_pages/get_page has a 'path' field (e.g. 'api-test-page') the harvester never captured; patched pr-api-tester/server.py's extract_first_id -> extract_first_id_and_path to also pull a sibling 'path' field from the same object and seed it under the '...Path' variant of the derived id key (e.g. pageId -> pagePath) -- needs MCP restart, so this run's result was instead confirmed by calling the live endpoint directly with explicit seed_ids and recording the real HTTP 200 into call-library-validated.json by hand. (3) sync_change_request -- confirmed live (fresh, untouched change request) that HTTP 409 {"error":{"code":409,"message":"Branch is already up-to-date"}} is GitBook's correct, documented response, not a call defect; added an 'expected_status_codes':[200,409] field to this entry in call-library.json and patched tag_result() in server.py to honor a per-entry expected_status_codes allowlist instead of blanket-failing every >=400 status -- also needs MCP restart, result recorded by hand from the live diagnostic call in the interim.
